Judgment.description: What a sentinel decided during one exchange, for an Inspect eval, which asks for it with `request_result`.

outcome.description: What the exchange came to: `proceed` when the reply goes on, `reject` when the model's turn was refused and the run goes on, and `terminate` when the run has ended, in this exchange or before it.
outcome.title: Outcome

trimmed.description: True when the sidecar was told not to send results, so each step holds only what Inspect acts on: its stage, its call, and its decision's action, message and modified call.
trimmed.title: Trimmed

steps.description: Every step judged during the exchange, in the order they were judged. A step that ended the run is the last. Empty when the run had already ended.
steps.title: Steps

withheld.description: The model's turn, when the client was refused it because a call in it was rejected, or because a sentinel ended the run at the reply or at a call in it.

proposed.description: The model's turn, when the client was handed it with calls taken out because they were rejected, or changed. Each call taken out is redacted, each changed call is as it ran, and `results` holds what the model is told of each call taken out. The sidecar puts those calls and results back in each later request of the conversation that doesn't already hold them.

usage.description: What the provider billed for the model's reply, as Inspect writes `ModelUsage`, when the client was refused a reply the model gave. A refusal carries no usage of its own, so the client counts it from here.

The sidecar keeps it once the registration succeeds, and never sends it back. A sidecar that keeps another token for the eval answers `unauthorized`.

It proves only that the caller holds the token, not the call's other parameters. Sent in place of the token once the sidecar holds it. A sidecar that holds no token for the eval answers `unknown_task`, and the eval registers again with its token.

title: Inspect Sentinel: the endpoint for evals
description: JSON-RPC 2.0 methods, POSTed to /sentinel/v1, with a probe at GET /sentinel/info. `methods` names the definitions that a method's `params` and `result` fit. `errors` lists the codes of the method errors of the endpoint's own.

-32001.name: registration_refused
-32001.description: The sidecar takes no tasks registered by an eval, and this task was not registered beforehand; or, for `complete_registration`, the sidecar takes only the samples a task's registration names, and this sample isn't one.

-32008.name: registrations_full
-32008.description: The sidecar keeps as many task registrations as it takes, and takes another once a kept one expires; or, for `complete_registration`, the task's registration holds as much as the sidecar takes for a task. A failure, not a refusal: the deployment has not said that the task may not run.

-32002.name: unknown_sample
-32002.description: The sidecar holds nothing for the sample, so an eval never mistakes a forgotten sample for a clean one.

-32009.name: unknown_task
-32009.description: The sidecar holds no registration of the task by the eval: it was never registered, or is no longer kept. The eval registers the task again, then completes the sample's registration. Answered to a `register_task` with a `mac` when the sidecar holds no token for the eval, as after a restart or once the token expired: the eval registers again with its token.

-32010.name: unauthorized
-32010.description: The call's `mac` isn't made with the token the sidecar keeps for the eval, or its `timestamp` is further from the sidecar's clock than the window allows; or a `register_task` sent another token than the one the sidecar keeps for the eval.
